title: Chain-of-Thought Prompting Elicits Reasoning in Large Language Models
layout_note: Two columns titled 'Standard Prompting' (left) and 'Chain-of-Thought Prompting' (right); each column stacks a tall 'Model Input' box over a short 'Model Output' box, so the two methods differ only in the highlighted text.
grouping: Each column is one method under a bold column title; within it, an input box and an output box are each tagged by a pill label on the top-left border (blue pill 'Model Input', green pill 'Model Output'). No background panels.
shapes_depth: Flat rounded rectangles with a thin grey outline and large corner radius; content is plain sans-serif prompt text (Q:/A: exemplars); pill-shaped coloured tags sit across the box borders.
proposed_highlight: The added reasoning steps are highlighted as text-marker backgrounds inside the right column: blue behind the chain of thought in the exemplar answer and green behind the model's generated reasoning; a green check mark versus a red cross on the outputs states the result.
lesson: When the method is a change to text, show the same prompt twice side by side and mark only the inserted words with a highlighter background in the colour of the box tag they belong to.
notes: venue from the first page (36th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems, NeurIPS 2022). Figure 1 is the paper's only method illustration; the other figures are result plots and example tables. Highlight colours match the pill tags: blue for input, green for output.

taxonomy.task: few-shot reasoning by prompting an LLM
taxonomy.note: family other = LLM prompting / in-context reasoning (no agent loop or environment); nearest family is llm-agent (Tree of Thoughts, Self-Refine)

insights.structure: Two equal columns, standard prompting left and chain-of-thought right, each a tall Model Input box over a short Model Output box, so the comparison is a strict before/after pair.
insights.data: Inputs and outputs are drawn as the literal Q:/A: prompt text (the tennis-ball and cafeteria-apples problems), not as abstract boxes, with a red cross after the wrong answer and a green check after the right one.
insights.emphasis: Only the inserted reasoning sentences carry colour, as blue (exemplar) and green (generated) highlighter backgrounds in the right column, matching the blue Model Input and green Model Output pill tags.
insights.flow: Read left column then right column, each top to bottom from input to output; there are no arrows, the vertical stacking alone implies input-then-output.

arrangement.units: two columns (standard vs chain-of-thought), each holding an outlined rounded Model Input box above an outlined rounded Model Output box, tagged by coloured pills
arrangement.inputs_as: quoted few-shot prompt text (Q:/A: exemplars and the test question)
arrangement.shared: the same question text is repeated verbatim in both columns

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)
